From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: MedVault — hosting & security follow-up

Emily / Devon —

Great to meet you both on the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

- Requirement summary (from call): HIPAA/BAA required; SOC2 evidence requested; preference toward Private VPC but evaluating Dedicated capacity for predictable throughput.
- Immediate asks from MedVault: list of SOC2 artifacts, sample BAA language, and architecture notes for Private VPC network topology.
- Redwood proposed path: start with a Hosted API pilot for low-sensitivity workloads + run a parallel Dedicated capacity benchmark for latency/cost. If BAA scope requires full separation, migrate to Private VPC with our private control plane.

Can Marissa share the SOC2/BAA artifact checklist? Karthik — can you confirm high-level latency and egress controls for Private VPC vs Dedicated?

Proposed next steps:
1) I’ll share Redwood’s standard BAA draft and SOC2 evidence index (attached).
2) MedVault to confirm whether PHI will be processed in pilot. If yes, we prioritize Private VPC.
3) Schedule a technical deep-dive (30–45m) next week to align on network, KMS, and audit window.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a calendar invite after receiving availability.

— Sergio

Thanks, Sergio — appreciate the clear recap. Two quick clarifications from our side: 

- We will be processing PHI in production, so BAA-covered environments are non-negotiable for any real traffic. Pilot can use de-identified data, but production must be BAA-compliant.
- Primary preference: Private VPC (our security team wants customer-controlled network + KMS integration). However, if Private VPC timeline is months, we need a path to Dedicated capacity that meets BAA contractually (and mitigations for logical separation).

Also: what is the expected turnaround for providing SOC2 Type II artifacts? Our security team will want to review evidence prior to procurement.

Happy to jump on the technical deep-dive — Devon and I are available Thurs 10:00–11:30 PT or Friday afternoon.

— Emily

Emily —

Thanks for the clarity. To make the SOC2/BAA review efficient, I’m attaching our SOC2 evidence index and a BAA draft (see attachments). For procurement, security typically needs the following artifacts during evaluation: 

- Most recent SOC2 Type II report (PDF) + auditor name and date range
- Control mapping (which controls map to PHI handling, encryption, access controls)
- Data retention and deletion policy + retention windows for logs
- KMS integration notes (supported HSM/KMS providers and key rotation cadence)
- Network topology diagram for Private VPC and Dedicated (how traffic egress is controlled)
- Incident response runbook / SLAs for incident notification

If MedVault wants to evaluate Dedicated first, we can provide an ATO-like package: a focused subset of SOC2 artifacts + a contractual BAA addendum that scopes dedicated instances. That would allow you to run a functional performance test while the Private VPC provisioning proceeds.

Attachments: BAA_Draft_MV_2028.docx, Redwood_SOC2_Index.pdf

I’ll join the technical deep-dive to cover artifact questions. Sergio — can you propose times per Emily’s availability?

Best,
Marissa Cole

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dr. Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@medvault.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Mar 2028 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MedVault — hosting & security follow-up

Emily / team —

Quick technical notes ahead of the deep-dive: 

- Private VPC: typical provision time is 3–6 weeks (depends on network peering & customer review cycle). Private control plane gives you VPC-native routing, direct peering options, and customer-managed KMS with full audit logs forwarded to your SIEM. Estimated latency: identical to our dedicated regional footprint; typically 10–25ms depending on region and instance type.

- Dedicated capacity: faster to stand up (2–5 days for initial pool). Provides reserved GPU capacity and tenancy isolation at the host/instance level but uses Redwood-managed control plane. Contractually we can bind a BAA piece and narrow SOC2 scoping for the dedicated pool; however logical separation vs physical (on-prem) is different. We recommend a short dedicated pilot if you need to validate latency/cost before full Private provisioning.

- Egress / data flow: for PHI we recommend explicit egress rules (deny by default) and enforcement via VPC gateway + private endpoints. We can provide sample iptables/nginx ACLs and Cloud NAT guidance during the deep-dive.

- Next actions before the call: Emily, please confirm whether the pilot will use de-identified or real PHI. If de-identified, we can run immediate hosted/dedicated benchmark; if PHI, we’ll escalate to priority Private VPC provisioning and pull in Solutions Engineering for design.

Happy to run a 45-minute technical session Thurs 10:30 PT if that still works — otherwise send a slot.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
